title: [bug] Asset protocol crashes app with large video files
body: When I seek near the end of longer or larger videos through Tauri's asset protocol, the video hangs and eventually crashes the app. My testing suggests file size is the deciding factor: a long but small countdown video works, while files larger than about 3.5 GiB crash when seeking roughly 80% into the file, when about 3 GiB would need to be loaded. Seeking also takes several seconds, which makes it look like the asset protocol loads everything from the start through the seek point; the same seek is instant through an HTTP range-streaming server. The process uses around 4 GB before crashing even though the machine has 32 GB of RAM. Tauri's streaming example behaves the same way. Nothing appears in DevTools or the tauri dev terminal when it crashes; with RUST_BACKTRACE set, it instead loads endlessly. Rocket with rocket_seek_stream avoids the crash and makes seeking instant, but I would rather not embed Rocket. I am on Windows 10 with WebView2 110, Tauri 1.2.4, Wry 0.23.4, Rust 1.66.1, and I linked a small reproduction repository that lets the user select a local video.

symptoms_visible: Seeking roughly 80% into a video larger than about 3.5 GiB hangs and eventually crashes my app.
Seeking through the asset protocol takes several seconds, while the same seek through my Rocket range-streaming workaround is instant.
The process reaches around 4 GB of RAM before it crashes; without a crash under RUST_BACKTRACE, the video instead keeps loading indefinitely.
N0.label: N0 large-video asset protocol crash reported

symptoms_visible: With the provided range-streaming protocol, seeking is instant and long or large videos no longer hang or crash.
The initial video load remains slightly slower than with Rocket.
N1.label: N1 initial range-stream patch works

symptoms_visible: After switching to the updated multipart implementation, streamed subtitle files begin with many NUL characters and no longer work.
N2_x.label: N2_x multipart update subtitle aftermath

symptoms_visible: The separate VTT subtitle response still starts with NUL characters under the updated implementation.
N3.label: N3 subtitle request details collected

symptoms_visible: After applying the corrected implementation, small videos, small videos with subtitles, large videos, and large videos with subtitles all work.
N4.label: N4 corrected streaming implementation verified

symptoms_visible: With the integrated development build, video streaming works, captions display correctly, and seeking is instant.
N_terminal.label: terminal integrated fix verified

solution.intent: Replace whole-file-style asset loading with a custom protocol implementation that parses HTTP Range requests, seeks directly to the requested byte offset, and returns the requested range rather than reading from the beginning through the seek point.
solution.concrete_example: Register a stream URI protocol that reads the Range header, seeks the file with SeekFrom::Start, returns 206 Partial Content with Content-Range and Accept-Ranges headers, and streams only the requested bytes.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter suspected start-to-seek loading from timing and memory behavior. Identifying proper HTTP byte-range streaming as the corrective mechanism is engineer-side reasoning, validated when the proposed implementation made large-file seeking instant and stable.

edges.comment: Opening report and c1-c2, reporter mauritzn's system: amrbashir supplied a range-aware stream protocol patch, and the reporter confirmed that large videos stopped hanging or crashing and seeks became instant.

solution.intent: Replace the initial range-streaming snippet with the updated multipart range implementation intended for temporary use until the integrated asset-protocol fix is released.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the maintainer's updated diff that adds multipart range handling to the custom stream protocol.

edges.comment: c5-c6, reporter mauritzn's system: the reporter applied the revised multipart implementation and then showed that it prefixed subtitle responses with NUL bytes. This exact revision is a falsified move, though the overall range-streaming direction remains correct.

question_patterns: Are the subtitles embedded in the video or stored separately, and how are they loaded?
What subtitle format and HTML mechanism are you using?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: They are separate .vtt files, not embedded in the video, and I stream them through the HTML <track> element.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The subtitles are embedded tracks inside the video container; there is no separate subtitle request.
They are separate WebVTT files loaded by multiple <track> elements rather than one.

question_patterns: Can you share the request and response details for the subtitle file?
What headers are present on the failing subtitle request?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not quite sure which details you need, but these are the request headers. They look the same as with the old implementation; the only difference I noticed is that the updated response has a content-length header.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated request contains a nonzero Range header for the middle of the VTT file, while the old request always requested the whole file.
The request was made from a different page route, but the headers and NUL-prefixed response are unchanged.

question_patterns: How do the old and updated protocol responses differ?
Do you see any header difference between the working and failing subtitle responses?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The request headers look the same to me. The only thing missing from the old version is content-length in the response headers.

edges.comment: c7-c11, reporter mauritzn's system: the maintainer asked whether subtitles were separate and requested network details. The reporter supplied first-person request evidence and then added a subtitle reproduction branch, recorded as volunteered target-node information.

solution.intent: Correct the multipart stream buffer allocation so capacity is reserved without inserting zero bytes before the data.
solution.concrete_example: Replace a buffer initialized as vec![0; len] with Vec::with_capacity(len), then write the streamed response bytes into the empty buffer.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer identified that vec![0; len] created len actual zero-valued bytes rather than merely reserving storage. The reporter supplied the NUL-prefixed output and request details but did not derive that allocation bug.

edges.comment: c13-c14, reporter mauritzn's system: amrbashir corrected the pre-allocation mistake, and the reporter tested small and large videos both with and without subtitles and confirmed all four cases worked.

solution.intent: Use the integrated Tauri asset-protocol implementation that streams requested byte ranges and includes the corrected buffer handling, then verify large-video seeking and captions on a build containing it.
solution.concrete_example: Move from the temporary custom Rocket server or local snippet to a Tauri build containing the integrated range-streaming asset protocol, then test seeking through a large local video and loading its separate VTT captions.

edges.comment: c21-c22: reporter mauritzn installed and tested the integrated development branch and reported instant seeking, working captions, and correct video streaming. A second affected user independently said it worked, but that separate operator's earlier runtime problem is not spliced into the reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted core diagnosis: the asset protocol needed proper HTTP byte-range streaming so a late seek reads the requested range instead of accumulating data from the start through the seek point.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the file-size and seek-position behavior, high memory use, instant Rocket range-streaming workaround, and successful range-streaming patch test.
Must preserve the subtitle fix: the multipart revision inserted NUL bytes because it created a zero-filled buffer with vec![0; len]; capacity must be reserved without adding bytes.
Must not recommend the faulty zero-filled multipart implementation as the fix, because it was tested and corrupted separate VTT subtitle responses.

The permanent recommendation should use Tauri's integrated range-streaming asset protocol rather than requiring the reporter to keep Rocket, while allowing the custom protocol as a temporary workaround.
Must ask the affected user to verify large-video seeking and captions on a build containing the integrated fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable application developer who can modify Rust and Cargo files, compare network headers, maintain reproduction branches, test development builds, and benchmark multi-gigabyte media files.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, cooperative, and appreciative; reports measured thresholds and comparison timings, tests patches promptly, supplies screenshots and reproduction branches, and clearly distinguishes major failures from minor performance concerns.
